claim: Security analyses that consider only individual stages of an LLM post-training pipeline systematically underestimate the overall vulnerability because compound effects from multiple stages can emerge only when stages are analyzed jointly.
falsifier: Design a security evaluation that compares per-stage red-teaming results with full-pipeline red-teaming on a different model family and task to test whether the underestimation holds.

conditions: pipeline consists of multiple post-training stages (e.g., SFT, DPO, PPO)
each stage can be independently poisoned
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported model, dataset, trigger, and experimental conditions; transfer to other models, tasks, or pipelines is unestablished.

title: Analyzing stages individually versus–estimated vulnerability boundary

claim: Post-training large language models with training data generated from a knowledge graph that models domain-specific legal concepts (IRAC framework) improves performance on legal reasoning benchmarks compared to baselines without such knowledge graph assistance.
falsifier: One could replicate the experiment by constructing an IRAC knowledge graph for a legal domain, generating training data from it, and post-training an LLM via SFT and DPO, then evaluating on legal benchmarks.

conditions: Post-training applied to mid-to-large LLMs (30B-70B parameters)
Training data generated from IRAC knowledge graph modeling legal concepts
Both SFT and DPO training methods used
exclusions: Evidence is limited to U.S. law (common law) and the reported experimental conditions; generalizability to other legal systems is unestablished.

title: Using a knowledge graph for average performance on legal

claim: Under the condition of in-flow boundary data as a small perturbation of a global Maxwellian, the steady Boltzmann equation with in-flow boundary condition converges to the incompressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier system with Dirichlet boundary condition.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by numerically solving the steady Boltzmann equation with in-flow boundary data set as a small perturbation of a global Maxwellian and verifying that the solution approaches the incompressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier system with Dirichlet boundary condition in the hydrodynamic limit.

conditions: in-flow boundary data is a small perturbation of a global Maxwellian
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the steady Boltzmann equation with in-flow boundary condition and the specific perturbation condition studied; transfer beyond these conditions is unestablished.

title: Steady Boltzmann equation–convergence to the incompressible theorem
